decisions.reason: The existing MODIFY reopens the second V as a copied-and-scaled Hero V but leaves two stale attributes prohibiting reuse of the Hero V's expressive right-arm geometry and leaves the prior locked-asset revision policy unchanged.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Abdulbari,

Thank you for restoring the foundation. I think we're much closer now.

Before we continue refining the alphabet, I'd like to revisit one aspect of the VvÉ system. Looking back at our earlier explorations, I prefer the hierarchy between the Hero V and the second V in concepts #2 and #3 (attached). I don't think the current proof has quite achieved that same relationship yet.

Will you please show these two options?

Option 1: Create the second V by copying the approved Hero V and reducing it proportionally as a single object (without redrawing it). It should remain a true scaled version of the Hero V while still extending above the E and L.

Option 2: Start with that same copied-and-scaled Hero V, then make only the minimal optical refinements you feel are necessary so it integrates more naturally with the alphabet while preserving the same identity and maintaining its elevation above the E and L.

Next, will you please refine the optical spacing throughout the word? I like the visual rhythm of the L–V relationship in this proof and would use that as the benchmark for balancing the remaining letter pairs.

I've attached the earlier concepts as a reference for the Hero V/second V relationship I'm referring to.

Thank you!

value_updates.derivation_rule: Create the second V from a copied, proportionally reduced approved Hero V as a single object.
geometry_options: The same copied-and-scaled Hero V with only minimal optical refinements that preserve its identity
value_updates.asset_status: reopened for the explicitly requested two-option refinement
value_updates.revision_policy: Preserve the approved Hero V identity while permitting only the requested exact proportional scaling or minimal optical refinement options for the second V.

The approved Hero V remains the unchanged source geometry; the requested alternatives apply only to the derived second V.
The existing same-message MODIFY already records that E and L exploration continues around the locked Hero V and É accent while the second V is evaluated under the two requested options.
Changing the second V derivation options does not alter the required peak alignment between the fixed Hero V and É accent.
The existing same-message MODIFY records the preferred concepts #2 and #3 hierarchy, while the established requirement that the second V remain elevated above E and L continues unchanged.
The source terminal-treatment decision does not itself change kerning, and the separate same-message spacing instruction is already represented by the L–V rhythm benchmark MODIFY.
The second V geometry decision does not change the deferred champagne material treatment or its role.
The source decision changes glyph treatment and does not alter the requirement to explain design rationale with review rounds.
The source decision has no effect on acceptable proof attachment formats.
